 UPSC Prelims Current Affairs for 17 November 2026
 by Vajiram & Ravi - 17 November 2026
 Vajiram & Ravi provides Daily UPSC Prelims Current Affairs for 17 November 2026, tailored for aspirants. We cover all relevant news and events crucial for the exam, ensuring you stay updated & well-prepared.
 India and UAE Hold Water Roundtable Ahead of 2026 UN Water Conference in Abu Dhabi 
 November 17, 2026 
 2026 UN Water Conference Latest News 
 The Embassy of the UAE in New Delhi recently convened the UAE-India Water Roundtable ahead of the 2026 UN Water Conference. 
 About 2026 UN Water Conference 
 It will take place from 8 to 10 December 2026 in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates (UAE ) . 
 It will be co-hosted by the Republic of Senegal and the UAE.   
 It aims to accelerate implementation of Sustainable Development Goal 6 (SDG 6) on water and sanitation , strengthen global water governance, and further elevate water-related issues on the international agenda.  
 The 2026 Conference will build on momentum from the UN 2023 Water Conference in New York , which was the first UN conference dedicated to water in nearly 50 years.  
 It is expected to bring together governments, the UN system, and stakeholders from across sectors to advance action on water and sanitation.  
 The theme for 2026 is " Delivering the Water Action Agenda: From Commitments to Action" , with a focus on scalable, measurable, and concrete solutions.   
 The 2026 UN Water Conference will feature plenary sessions and six interactive dialogues on the following themes: 
 Water for People 
 Water for Prosperity 
 Water for Planet 
 Water for Cooperation 
 Water for Multilateral processes 
 Investments for water 
 News: ANI 
 2026 UN Water Conference FAQ's
 Q1: When will the 2026 UN Water Conference be held?
 Ans: From 8 to 10 December 2026.
 Q2: Where will the 2026 UN Water Conference be held?
 Ans: Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates (UAE).
 Q3: Which countries will co-host the 2026 UN Water Conference?
 Ans: The Republic of Senegal and the United Arab Emirates.
 Q4: What are the major objectives of the 2026 UN Water Conference?
 Ans: To accelerate the implementation of SDG 6, strengthen global water governance, and elevate water-related issues on the international agenda.
 Q5: What is the theme of the 2026 UN Water Conference?
 Ans: “Delivering the Water Action Agenda: From Commitments to Action”.
 Adani Ports, MEIL Among Bidders for ₹11,733 Crore V.O. Chidambaranar Port Expansion Project 
 November 17, 2026 
 V.O. Chidambaranar Port Latest News 
 Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone, Megha Engineering and Infrastructure (MEIL), and Vishwa Samudra Engineering are competing for the Rs. 117.33 bn outer harbour infrastructure project at VO Chidambaranar (VOC) Port in Thoothukudi. 
 About V.O. Chidambaranar Port 
 V.O. Chidambaranar Port ( formerly Tuticorin Port ) is an all-weather major seaport located in the Gulf of Mannar in Thoothukudi, in South Tamil Nadu.   
 It is an artificial deep-sea harbour.  
 It is positioned strategically close to the international East-West shipping channel. 
 The inner harbour has 14 berths, including 3 coal and oil jetties and 2 container jetties.  
 The port manages both cruise ships and containers.  
 It has the capacity to handle 81.50 Million Tonnes of cargo per year. 
 V.O. Chidambaranar Port History 
 The history of Tuticorin Port dates back as early as 123 AD, when Ptolemy from Greece described Tuticorin as a flourishing trade centre engaged in maritime trade with Western and Eastern countries.   
 Tuticorin was declared as a minor anchorage port in 1868 .   
 After Independenc e, the minor port of Tuticorin witnessed a flourishing trade and handled a variety of cargo meant for the neighbouring countries and the coastal regions of India.  
 To cope with the increasing trade through Tuticorin, the Government of India sanctioned the construction of an all-weather port at Tuticorin.  
 In July 1974 , the newly constructed Tuticorin Port   was declared as the 10th Major Port of India.  
 On 1st April 1979 , the erstwhile Tuticorin minor port and the newly constructed Tuticorin major port were merged, and the Tuticorin Port Trust was constituted under the Major Port Trusts Act of 1963.  
 Given the history of the freedom struggle in Tuticorin, the Tuticorin Port Trust was renamed as V.O. Chidambaranar Port Trus t on 19th February 2011 , in honour of freedom fighter V.O. Chidambaram Pillai.  
 It was renamed as V.O. Chidambaranar Port Authority on 31.01.2022, an autonomous body constituted under the Major Port Authorities Act 2021 by the Central Government.  
 It functions under the administrative control of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. 
 News: CW 
 V.O. Chidambaranar Port FAQs
 Q1: Where is V.O. Chidambaranar Port located?
 Ans: In Thoothukudi, in southern Tamil Nadu.
 Q2: What was the former name of V.O. Chidambaranar Port?
 Ans: Tuticorin Port.
 Q3: What type of port is V.O. Chidambaranar Port?
 Ans: An all-weather major seaport and artificial deep-sea harbour.
 Q4: Which international shipping route is V.O. Chidambaranar Port strategically located close to?
 Ans: The international East–West shipping channel.
 Q5: What is the administrative status of V.O. Chidambaranar Port Authority?
 Ans: It is an autonomous body constituted by the Central Government.
 India Revises Maritime Flag Rules After 65 Years, Mandates Red and Blue Ensigns for Ships 
 November 17, 2026 
 Revised Maritime Flag Rules Latest News 
 India recently introduced a new set of rules governing the flags flown by Indian ships at sea, replacing a notification that had remained in force for more than six decades. 
 About Revised Maritime Flag Rules 
 The new rules have been notified under Section 37(1) of the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025, superseding the earlier order dated February 9, 1961 .   
 With the new notification, the Centre has replaced the maritime flag framework that had governed Indian vessels since 1961. 
 The new rules establish separate flag requirements for merchant ships, government-owned vessels, and ships operating exclusively for the Ministry of Defence.  
 However, actions already taken under the earlier notification will continue to remain valid.  
 Revised Rules for Indian Merchant Ships: 
 All Indian merchant vessels registered under the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025, will be required to fly the Red Ensign.  
 The flag will be red, with the Indian National Flag placed in the upper canton, the area closest to the flagstaff.  
 Its length will be one and a half times its width, in accordance with the Flag Code of India, 2002. 
 Revised Rules for Government-Owned Vessels:  
 They will fly the Blue Ensig n, irrespective of whether they are registered under the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025.  
 These vessels will carry the official badge of the government department, authority, or organisation that owns them.   
 However, the provision specifically excludes ships belonging to the Indian Navy and the Indian Coast Guard.  
 The government has also laid down rules for the use of official badges on the Blue Ensign.  
 Any new badge will require prior approval from the Centre , with applications routed through the Director General of Maritime Administration.  
 Organisations already using an approved badge will be allowed to continue with it.  
 Revised Rules for Merchant Vessels Operating Exclusively for the Defence Ministry: 
 A separate category has been created for Indian merchant vessels that receive financial assistance from the Ministry of Defence and operate exclusively for the ministry.  
 These vessels will also be required to fly the Blue Ensign instead of the Red Ensign.   
 However, their badges will need to be authorised through a Warrant issued by the Chief of the Naval Staff.  
 Applications for such approval will have to be submitted directly to the Naval Chief.  
 Specifications for the Blue Ensign: 
 The flag will have a royal blue background , with the Indian National Flag positioned in the upper canton.   
 The badge , in light golden colour, will be placed at the centre of the fly half of the flag, the portion farthest from the flagstaff.  
 The badge must fit within a circular area whose diameter cannot exceed 13/30th of the flag's width.  
 What Does Section 37 of the Merchant Shipping Act Says? 
 Section 37 of the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025, empowers the Central Government to notify the appropriate national colours for Indian vessels and government-owned ships, including different flags for different categories of vessels. 
 The provision also requires registered Indian vessels to hoist their prescribed national colours when signalled by an Indian Navy or Coast Guard vessel, as well as when entering or leaving a port. 
 It further authorises commissioned Navy officers, Coast Guard officers, surveyors and Indian ambassadors to board vessels flying colours in violation of the Act and seize such flags, which can be forfeited to the government. 
 The law also prohibits foreign vessels from using Indian national colours to falsely present themselves as Indian ships, except in specific circumstances involving escape from capture during hostilities. 
 News: NDTV 
 Revised Maritime Flag Rules FAQs
 Q1: Under which legislation have the Revised Maritime Flag Rules been notified?
 Ans: Under Section 37(1) of the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025.
 Q2: Which categories of vessels are covered under the revised maritime flag rules?
 Ans: Indian merchant ships, government-owned vessels and merchant vessels operating exclusively for the Ministry of Defence.
 Q3: Which ensign must Indian merchant ships registered under the Merchant Shipping Act, 2025, fly?
 Ans: The Red Ensign.
 Q4: Which ensign must government-owned vessels fly under the revised maritime flag rules?
 Ans: The Blue Ensign.
 Q5: What must government-owned vessels display on the Blue Ensign?
 Ans: The official badge of the government department, authority or organisation that owns them.
 Scientists Discover New Moss Species Macromitrium nelliampathyanum in Kerala’s Nelliampathy Hills 
 November 17, 2026 
 Macromitrium Nelliampathyanum Latest News 
 Recently, an international team of botanists has discovered a brand-new species of moss and named it Macromitrium nelliampathyanum. 
 About Macromitrium Nelliampathyanum 
 It is a new moss species discovered in Keralam. 
 The discovery took place approximately 1,400 metres above sea level atop Hill Top Mount in the Nelliampathy Hills, located within the Palakkad District of Kerala. 
 It belongs to the genus Macromitrium, a diverse family of mosses typically found draping trees and rocks across tropical regions. 
 The species has been named Macromitrium nelliampathyanum directly in honour of its type locality, the Nelliampathy Hills. 
 Features 
 When dried out, its narrow leaves curl and twist dramatically along their midribs. 
 When reproducing, the moss produces a tiny, globe-like spore capsule topped with a pleated hood that bears a few hairs at its tip. 
 It also demonstrates true anisospory, meaning a single capsule produces spores in two distinctly different size classes. 
 Source: RM 
 Macromitrium Nelliampathyanum FAQs
 Q1: What is Macromitrium Nelliampathyanum?
 Ans: Moss
 Q2: Where was Macromitrium Nelliampathyanum discovered?
 Ans: It was discovered in Keralam.
 India Hosts 62nd International Coconut Community Ministerial Meeting in Kochi, Kerala 
 November 17, 2026 
 International Coconut Community Latest News 
 India is hosting the 62nd Session and Ministerial Meeting of the International Coconut Community (ICC) at Kochi, Kerala.  
 About International Coconut Community      
 It was established in 1969 under the aegis of the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UN-ESCAP). 
 It is an inter-governmental organisation of   coconut-producing countries. 
 It provides a common platform for member countries to deliberate on issues concerning the development of the global coconut sector, promote cooperation and partnerships , and explore opportunities for the sustainable growth of the coconut industry. 
 Functions 
 It facilitates measures to increase global coconut production and productivity. 
 It collaborates with existing international bodies to reduce trade barriers and restrictions. 
 It facilitates training of member countries on relevant aspects of coconut development. 
 It harmonizes quality standards for coconut products and assist members to meet these standards. 
 It assists member countries mobilize resources by linking them with potential donor institutions as needed. 
 Member Countries: It currently has 21 coconut producing member countries accounting for over 90 percent of world coconut production and exports of coconut products. 
 India is also a member country of this organization 
 Secretariat : The ICC Secretariat is located in Jakarta, Indonesia 
 Source: PIB 
 International Coconut Community FAQs
 Q1: What is International Coconut Community?
 Ans: It was established in 1969 under the aegis of the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (UN-ESCAP).
 Q2: Where is International Coconut Community's secretariat is located?
 Ans: Jakarta, Indonesia
 Adi Vaani Platform Launched in Mysuru as India’s First AI-Powered Tribal Language Translator 
 November 17, 2026 
 Adi Vaani Latest News 
 Adi Vaani has established an initial digital foundation for tribal languages through translation tools, educational resources and community-generated language data. 
 About Adi Vaani 
 It is India’s first AI-powered translator for tribal languages. 
 It is designed to bridge communication gaps between tribal and non-tribal communities, while safeguarding endangered tribal languages using advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI). 
 It was developed by a national consortium led by IIT Delhi , along with BITS Pilani, IIIT Hyderabad, IIIT Nava Raipur and the Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs) of Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Meghalaya. 
 AI Language Models: Refined deployment of models such as No Language Left Behind (NLLB) and IndicTrans2 for low-resource tribal languages. 
 It aims to 
 Enable real-time translation (text and speech) between Hindi/English and tribal languages. 
 Provide interactive language learning for students and early learners. 
 Digitally preserve folklore, oral traditions, and cultural heritage. 
 Support digital literacy, healthcare communication, and civic inclusion in tribal communities. 
 Awareness of the government schemes and important speeches 
 Features of Adi Vani 
 Audio files to Text: It transcribes live speech or audio files into text and translates into indigenous languages instantly. 
 Speech to speech Translation: Speak or upload speech in English or Hindi and listen to real-time voice translation in Santali, Mundari, or Bhili. 
 Text-to-text translation: Translation between supported tribal languages and languages such as Hindi and English. 
 Speech-to-text: Converts spoken words into text, supporting oral-language documentation. 
 Speech-to-speech translation: Translates speech by linking speech recognition, translation and speech synthesis. 
 Optical Character Recognition (OCR): Extracts text from images and scanned documents for translation. 
 Video subtitling: Supports translation of video content and public information into tribal languages. 
 Digital dictionaries and primers: Provide vocabulary, meanings and basic learning resources. 
 Source: PIB 
 Adi Vaani FAQs
 Q1: What is Adi Vaani?
 Ans: It is India’s first AI-powered translator for tribal languages.
 Q2: What is the function of Adi Vaani ?
 Ans: It is designed to bridge communication gaps between tribal and non-tribal communities, while safeguarding endangered tribal languages using advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI).
 DRDO and IAF Successfully Flight-Test RudraM-II Missile with 300 km Strike Range 
 November 17, 2026 
 RudraM-II Missile Latest News 
 Adani Defence and Aerospace (a production partner) recently said that the RudraM-II, an indigenous air-to-surface missile developed by the DRDO, is nearing production clearance and will soon be prepared for the export market. 
 About RudraM-II Missile 
 It is an indigenously-developed solid-propelled air-to-surface missile system. 
 It has been indigenously developed by Research Centre Imarat, Hyderabad as the nodal DRDO laboratory in collaboration with other sister labs. 
 It is designed primarily for Suppression of Enemy Air Defences (SEAD) and Destruction of Enemy Air Defences (DEAD) missions.   
 RudraM-II Missile Features 
 It can reach a peak speed of Mach 5.5. 
 It is capable of striking targets at a distance of approximately 300 km. 
 It can carry a warhead weighing up to 200 kg. 
 It can be deployed from aircraft like Sukhois flying at altitudes ranging from 3 to 15 km. 
 It acts as a key force multiplier and intends to eventually replace the older Russian-origin Kh-31 anti-radiation missiles. 
 It uses a hybrid navigation system combining an inertial navigation system, GPS and a sophisticated passive homing head that detects radio frequency emissions across a wide frequency band. 
 News: MI 
 RudraM-II Missile FAQs
 Q1: What is the RudraM-II missile?
 Ans: It is an indigenously developed, solid-propellant, air-to-surface missile system.
 Q2: Which organisation has developed the RudraM-II missile?
 Ans: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO).
 Q3: Which is the nodal DRDO laboratory responsible for developing the RudraM-II missile?
 Ans: Research Centre Imarat (RCI), Hyderabad, in collaboration with other DRDO laboratories.
 Q4: What are the primary operational objectives of the RudraM-II missile?
 Ans: Suppression of Enemy Air Defences (SEAD) and Destruction of Enemy Air Defences (DEAD).
 Q5: What is the approximate operational range of the RudraM-II missile?
 Ans: Approximately 300 km.
 Climate Change Performance Index 2026: India Slips 13 Places to 23rd Rank 
 November 17, 2026 
 Climate Change Performance Index Latest News 
 India has been ranked 28th in the recent Climate Change Performance Index 2027.  
 About Climate Change Performance Index 
 It tracks the progress of the world’s largest emitters in terms of emissions, renewables, and climate policy. 
 It was first published in 2005. 
 Global coverage: CCPI 2027 covers 64 countries and the EU, which together produce over 90% of global greenhouse gas emissions. 
 Assessment framework: Uses 14 indicators in four categories : Greenhouse Gas Emissions, Renewable Energy, Energy Use and Climate Policy. Around 500 climate and energy experts contribute to the policy assessment. 
 Main objective: Identifies countries making progress and those falling behind, and checks whether national actions align with the Paris Agreement goal of limiting warming to 1.5°C. 
 It is published by think tanks German watch, New Climate Institute , and Climate Action Network International. 
 Key Highlights of Climate Change Performance Index 2027 
 Top three ranks vacant: No country achieved a ‘Very High’ rating, showing that even the best performers are not meeting Paris Agreement goals. 
 Denmark (4th, 84.05 points): Top-ranked for the sixth consecutive year, driven by emission cuts and renewable energy progress. 
 G20 performance: The UK is the only G20 country with a ‘High’ rating, while ten G20 countries are rated ‘Very Low’. 
 India (28th, ‘Medium’): Down five places from 23rd (CCPI 2026) and 10th (CCPI 2025). 
 European Union (19th, ‘Medium’): Up one place. France (20th) and Germany (25th) are also in the medium category. 
 Lowest ranked: Iran (68th), USA (67th), Russia (66th), Saudi Arabia (65th), UAE (64th), all due to fossil fuel dependence. 
 Source: News On Air 
 Climate Change Performance Index FAQs
 Q1: What Climate Change Performance Index ?
 Ans: It tracks the progress of the world’s largest emitters in terms of emissions, renewables, and climate policy.
 Q2: When was Climate Change Performance Index first launched?
 Ans: 2005
 Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve Plans Enclosure to Care for Injured and Orphaned Tiger Cubs 
 November 17, 2026 
 Nagarjunagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve Latest News 
 The Central and State governments have proposed an alternative elevated corridor to ease night-time vehicle movement restrictions through the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve (NSTR) while ensuring wildlife conservation. 
 About Nagarjunagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve 
 It is located in the Nallamala hill ranges (an offshoot of the Eastern Ghats) of Andhra Pradesh. 
 With a total area of around 3568 sq.km., it is the largest tiger reserve in India and has the largest Critical Tiger Habitat area.  
 It is named after two major dams in the area, Nagarjuna Sagar Dam and Srisailam Dam. 
 Two wildlife sanctuaries, namely Rajiv Gandhi Wildlife Sanctuary and Gundla Brahmeswaram Wildlife Sanctuary (GBM), constitute the NSTR. 
 Topography : It consists of plateaus, ridges, gorges, and deep valleys. 
 Rivers : Krishna River is the major water source, with tributaries like Dindi, Peddavagu, and others.  
 The reserve holds significant importance with ancient temples like the Mallikarjuna Swamy Temple at Srisailam and several archaeological sites, including Buddhist relics from the Nagarjuna Konda area. 
 Tribes: Chenchu and Lambada tribal  communities maintain their ancestral relationship with the Nallamala forest. 
 Vegetation : It mainly consists of tropical dry deciduous forests having an undergrowth of bamboo and grass. 
 Flora : The habitat has several endemics like Andrographis nallamalayana, Eriolaena lushingtonii, Crotalaria madurensis Var, Dicliptera beddomei, and Premna hamiltonii. 
 Fauna : Tiger, Leopard, Wolf, Wild Dog, Jackal, Sambar, Chital, Chowsingha, Chinkara, Mouse Deer, Wild boar, and Porcupine etc. 
 News: NIE 
 Nagarjunagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve FAQs
 Q1: In which Indian state is the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve (NSTR) located?
 Ans: Andhra Pradesh.
 Q2: In which hill ranges is the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve located?
 Ans: The Nallamala Hill Ranges, an offshoot of the Eastern Ghats.
 Q3: Which is the major river flowing through the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve?
 Ans: Krishna River.
 Q4: What type of forests are predominantly found in the Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve?
 Ans: Tropical dry deciduous forests.
 Belarus: India and Belarus Hold 12th Inter-Governmental Commission Meeting in New Delhi 
 November 17, 2026 
 Belarus Latest News 
 The 12th Session of the India–Belarus Inter-Governmental Commission on Trade, Economic, Scientific, Technological and Cultural Cooperation was held in New Delhi. 
 About Belarus 
 Location: It is a landlocked country located in Eastern Europe . 
 Bordering Countries:   It is bordered by Russia in the north and east; by Ukraine in the south; by Poland in the west; by Lithuania and Latvia in the northwest. 
 Capital City: Minsk 
 Geographical Features of Belarus 
 Terrain: Much of the country consists of flat lowlands separated by low level-topped hills and uplands. About 40% of the country is forested 
 Climate: It has a cool continental climate moderated by maritime influences from the Atlantic Ocean. 
 Rivers: It is mainly drained by the river Dnieper and Mukhavyets, a tributary of the Bug (Buh) River, which forms part of the border with Poland and flows to the Baltic Sea. 
 Natural Resources: It mainly consists of peat deposits, forests, oil, natural gas, brown coal, fertile land, limestone, Iron. 
 Source: PIB 
 Belarus FAQs
 Q1: What is the capital of Belarus?
 Ans: Minsk
 Q2: Where is Belarus located?
 Ans: It is a landlocked country located in Eastern Europe.
